artifacts.synopsis: TE Aaron Myers appealed Illiana Presbytery's decision to elevate his censures from indefinite suspension from office and from the Sacraments to excommunication and deposition, without any additional judicial process. The SJC sustained the appeal 21-1, holding that due process principles require some form of process before censure may be elevated, though the majority held that full de novo judicial process was not required; the sole dissent (RE Eggert) argued that Traditional Process under the BCO Rules of Discipline was required, and a concurring opinion (Sartorius) also argued for full BCO process.

artifacts.synopsis: Central Carolina Presbytery remanded complaints to an Interim Session Commission rather than adjudicating them directly. The SJC confirmed this action, finding that the Commission appointed as Interim Session was the proper court of original jurisdiction and remanding the complaints for adjudication by that Commission.

artifacts.title: Granting constitutional status to BCO 53 on preaching

matches.evidence: The CCB found no constitutional conflict in an overture to grant constitutional status to BCO 53 governing the ministry of preaching.

artifacts.title: Prohibiting women's exhortation, preaching, or teaching in worship

matches.evidence: The CCB found that amending BCO 53 to expressly disallow women from exhorting, preaching, or teaching in corporate worship is not in conflict with the BCO.

artifacts.title: Disqualifying same-sex attracted men from ordination under BCO 7

matches.evidence: An overture from Westminster Presbytery to amend BCO 7 and related provisions disqualifying same-sex attracted men from ordination was found in conflict and adopted.

artifacts.title: Ordination ban for men self-identifying as gay Christians

matches.evidence: The CCB found this overture to amend BCO 17 prohibiting ordination of men using gay-identity labels to be in conflict with existing BCO provisions, though it was adopted.

artifacts.title: Overture defining roles of unordained deaconesses and deacon assistants

matches.evidence: CCB found Grace Presbytery's overture on deaconesses and women officers in conflict with the Constitution, noting the session, not the congregation, is the appointing body requiring vows.

artifacts.title: Proposed Revision of BCO 59 Marriage Language and Consent

matches.evidence: The CCB found Calvary Presbytery's overture to revise BCO 59 in conflict with the Constitution, as proposed changes to marriage publication and consent conflicted with BCO Preliminary Principle 7, BCO 11-2, BCO 29-1, and WCF 20.2.

artifacts.title: Granting BCO chapter 59 on marriage full constitutional status

matches.evidence: A Calvary Presbytery overture to elevate BCO 59 to full constitutional status was in conflict because doing so is equivalent to amending the BCO and requires the same multi-stage approval process under BCO 26-2.

artifacts.title: Proposed Procedure for Resolving Alleged Conflicts Between Scripture and the Constitution

matches.evidence: The CCB found Eastern Canada Presbytery's overture in conflict with the Constitution because it would allow a General Assembly to bypass constitutional processes and permit modification of commission reports.
